definitions.explanation: To move or act quickly because of limited time. Can be used intransitively (to be in a hurry) or transitively (to hurry something along).

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.notes: {急|いそ}いで is the te-form, commonly used as 'quickly'

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遅|おく}れる→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、{急|いそ}がなければならない。
examples.english: I'll miss the train, so I have to hurry.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで⟦{朝|あさ}ごはん→朝ご飯：02843_asagohan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate breakfast in a hurry.
examples.notes: {急|いそ}いで + verb = do something hurriedly

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: Both {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive) and {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: {急|いそ}ぐ (hurry, be in a hurry—intransitive) / Xを{急|いそ}ぐ (hurry X along—transitive, less common).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing state. {急|いそ}いでいる = 'is in a hurry' or 'is rushing.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{急|いそ}いで (in a hurry—te-form used adverbially)
・{急|いそ}がなくてもいい (don't need to hurry)
・{急|いそ}いでいる (is in a hurry)
・{仕事|しごと}を{急|いそ}ぐ (hurry the work along)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{急|いそ}ぎの{用事|ようじ} (urgent business)
・お{急|いそ}ぎですか (Are you in a hurry? - polite)

CAUTION: {急|いそ}ぐ implies physical hurrying. For 'time is running out' or 'urgent,' use {急|きゅう} (na-adjective) instead.
